title: Giant elliptical galaxy NGC 1316 in Fornax Cluster
caption: The central area of the giant elliptical galaxy NGC 1316, imaged by the Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 1316 · constellation Fornax · about 60 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Dark clouds and lanes of dust cross the heart of NGC 1316. This giant elliptical galaxy belongs to the Fornax cluster of galaxies. Scattered around it are objects that look like stars, and some of them are in fact globular clusters, dense balls of stars that belong to the galaxy.

Elliptical galaxies are usually smooth, rounded collections of stars with little dust, so the many dust clouds in the center of NGC 1316 make it stand out. The globular clusters around it are part of the galaxy's own family of stars.

Some features come from the camera, not the sky. Pyramid shapes above and below the bright center, and straight vertical streaks through several of the brightest stars, appear because those parts of the detector were overexposed, an effect known as CCD bleeding. The picture uses exposures from the 8.2-m VLT ANTU telescope and its FORS-1 instrument, taken through B, V and I filters that are rendered in blue, green-yellow and red.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.47 x 6.49 arcminutes) and distance (60 million light years), the frame spans roughly 113,000 × 113,000 light-years. Its light set out about 60 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The FORS-1 instrument on the 8.2-m VLT ANTU telescope recorded NGC 1316 through B, V and I filters. B is shown as blue, V as green-yellow and the near-infrared I filter as red.
understand.eye: The I filter records near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and the camera gathers far more light than the eye, so dust lanes and faint clusters stand out clearly.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The field measures 6.8 by 6.8 arcminutes, with 0.2 arcseconds per pixel, and the image quality of the composite is about 0.9 arcseconds. North is up and east is to the left. NGC 1316 lies about 60 million light-years away.
alt: The bright center of a giant elliptical galaxy crossed by dark dust lanes, with star-like globular clusters around it and pyramid-shaped overexposure artifacts above and below the center.
